I just watched Birdman and Nightcrawler back to back and both had so smooth mirror shots and I wondered where the camera went :D
How do directors/editors remove the camera from mirrors.

They could have taken a picture of the mirror with nothing else in the room, shopped the camera out of that one picture, and then after filming, replace the mirror in the scene with the mirror from the single photo.

Or, they just shopped it out on every single frame, but that would be super hard.
I don't believe that's what's happening since especially in Birdman the camera is hand operated and passes the mirror multiple times.

So there is a lens that can achieve this effect. It's called a tilt-shift lens. Here's an example.

The wikipedia article:

Another use of shifting is in taking pictures of a mirror. By moving the camera off to one side of the mirror, and shifting the lens in the opposite direction, an image of the mirror can be captured without the reflection of the camera or photographer. Shifting can similarly be used to photograph “around” an object, such as a building support in a gallery, without producing an obviously oblique view.

/v/newsubverses is good for both new subs and newly claimed abandoned subs, but what else is there, and how often is OK to make reposts, or rather are there other subs like /v/newsubverses which you can continue to promote your sub in.

Any tips for plugging your subverse in discussions around the site, without coming over as spamming your sub. Whats acceptable?
New rules may come in where if a sub gets no posts in 30 days, it will be deleted. Admin suggests promoting your sub has to be a regular activity for mods. How best to do this?

I think its reasonable to expect that a mod must make the first few posts, as its unreasonable to expect people to subscribe if there is no content there. But you do want at least half your content to be user submitted, how to encourage that?

For starters similar subverses could promote each other. I mod /v/steamsupport and have quick links to different gaming subverses in the sidebar. That way more active subverses redirect some of the traffic to more niche subs.

You could also mention your sebverse in relevant discussions across this site and others.

Other then that the best thing to do is to update the sub with content yourself so that when people stumble upon it they find it good enough to subscribe.

Yeah, so like mod relations get built, and sidebar link exchanges and stuff. I started out badmouthing /v/videos /r/videos in the same breath, saying 90% of it is vines and viral clips, without meaning to attack the sub or its mods, i may have shot myself in the foot for asking for sidebar, by being a bit offensive about that.

Also theres a feel from a much bigger sub, that helping out a smaller sub is a big ask, or a favor, which it is, they stand to gain nothing from using their sidebar for promoting an alternative (where the small sub gains a lot from the exchange), it has to be an act of good will.

Respect to you for doing that yourself of your own volition.

I just wanna say mentioning your sub(s) around in discussions is good, so is asking for your sub to be put in the featured subs rotation on the front page, that got me about half my subs i think. If you do make sure you get the sub looking/feeling finished before you do.
